question: Which of the following is an aspartic acid-containing dipeptide sweetener?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alitame.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​Alitame is an aspartic acid-containing dipeptide sweetener.
 
• It was developed by Pfizer in the early 1980s and is currently marketed in some countries under the brand name Aclame.
 
• Artificial sweetener: as an alternative to sucrose, some artificial sweetener is used.
 
• The diabetic patient can’t take sucrose, but this sweetener can be taken.
 
• It does not take part in biochemical reactions in the body.
 
• And also don’t produce calories in the body.
 
• So these are called calorie-free sweeteners.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__Sucralose__:

__
 
• Sucralose is an artificial sweetener and sugar substitute.
 
• The majority of ingested sucralose is not broken down by the body, so it is noncaloric. 

Saccharin: __

 
• Saccharin is an artificial sweetener with effectively no nutritional value.
 
• It is about 550 times as sweet as sucrose but has a bitter or metallic aftertaste, especially at high concentrations.
